item.title: 1986: Mets Rally Past Red Sox 8-5 in Game 7, Win Series
item.description: At Shea Stadium, the Mets come from behind again, overcoming a three-run Boston lead with six unanswered runs in the sixth and seventh innings and winning Game 7 of the World Series over the Red Sox by a final of 8–5. The Mets capture their second Fall Classic championship and first since 1969. Third baseman Ray Knight, whose homer broke a 3–3 deadlock in the seventh, is chosen Series MVP. Photo: Craig Johnson from San Diego, CA, USA (CC BY-SA 2.0).

item.title: 2023: Diamondbacks Beat Phillies 4-2, Return to World Series
item.description: After beating the Philadelphia Phillies 4–2 in Game 7 of the 2023 NLCS at Citizens Bank Park in Philadelphia, the Diamondbacks returned to the World Series for the first time since 2001 – against the Texas Rangers on October 27, 2023. Photo: Casey Aguinaldo (CC BY-SA 4.0).

item.title: 2020: Dodgers Beat Rays 3-1, Win 2020 World Series in Six
item.description: At Globe Life Field in Arlington, Texas the Los Angeles Dodgers defeat the Tampa Bay Rays 3–1 in Game 6 of the 2020 World Series to win the series 4–2. Corey Seager wins the World Series MVP. Photo: Michael Barera (CC BY-SA 4.0).

item.title: 2018: Red Sox Rally for 9-6 Win Over Dodgers, Lead Series 3-1
item.description: The Boston Red Sox rallied from a four-run deficit and scored nine runs in the final three innings, to defeat the Los Angeles Dodgers, 9–6, in Game 4 of the World Series at Dodger Stadium and take a 3–1 lead in the best-of-seven set. Mitch Moreland sparked the rally with a three-run home run off reliever Ryan Madson in the seventh inning. Photo: Keith Allison from Hanover, MD, USA (CC BY-SA 2.0).

item.title: 2017: Astros Beat Dodgers 5-3, Take 2-1 World Series Lead
item.description: The Houston Astros defeated the Los Angeles Dodgers at Minute Maid Park, 5–3, to take a 2–1 advantage in the World Series.

item.title: 2015: Royals Outlast Mets 5-4 in 14-Inning Game 1 Marathon
item.description: The Kansas City Royals outlasted the New York Mets in a 14-inning, five-hour, nine-minute marathon, to win Game One of the World Series by a score of 5–4 at Kauffman Stadium. Alcides Escobar connected a leadoff, first pitch inside-the-park home run; Eric Hosmer hit a game-winning sacrifice fly, and Chris Young, who was scheduled to open Game Four, pitched three hitless innings of relief along with four strikeouts. Photo: Arturo Pardavila III from Hoboken, NJ, USA (CC BY 2.0).

item.title: 2012: Giants Blank Tigers 2-0, Earn Consecutive Series Shutouts
item.description: Behind Ryan Vogelsong, Tim Lincecum, and Sergio Romo, the San Francisco Giants shut out the Detroit Tigers 2–0 in Game 3 of the World Series at Comerica Park. Having shut out the Tigers in Game 2 as well, the Giants become the first team since the Baltimore Orioles in 1966 to pitch consecutive shutouts in the World Series. Photo: Michael Marconi (CC BY 2.0).

item.title: 2011: Cardinals Win 11-Inning Game 6 Thriller on Freese Homer
item.description: The St. Louis Cardinals win a memorable Game 6 of the 2011 World Series in 11 innings. They trailed twice by two runs, in both the 9th and 10th innings, yet came back to tie the game, and then win it in the 11th inning on a David Freese solo home run leading off the inning, to dead centerfield. Photo: shgmom56 on Flickr (Original version) UCinternational (Crop) (CC BY-SA 2.0).

item.title: 2011: Angels to Hire Jerry Dipoto as General Manager
item.description: On October 27, 2011, it was reported that the Angels will hire Jerry Dipoto to serve as the franchise's eleventh general manager, there will be an official announcement by the Angels on October 28.

item.title: 2008: Rain Suspends Game 5 of World Series, First in History
item.description: Game 5 of the World Series in Philadelphia is suspended due to rain in the middle of the sixth inning with the Phillies and Rays tied 2–2 and the Phillies leading the series 3 games to 1. It is the first suspended game in World Series history. Photo: Edg126 (CC BY-SA 3.0).

item.title: 2006: Cardinals Beat Tigers 4-2, Win World Series 4-1
item.description: The St. Louis Cardinals defeat the Detroit Tigers 4–2, winning the World Series 4–1 for their 10th championship and their first since 1982. Their 83 regular-season victories is a new record for the fewest by a Series champion in a full season. Photo: Eric Draper (Public domain).

item.title: 2006: 83-Win Cardinals Upset Heavily Favored Tigers in Five Games
item.description: The postseason began on October 3, 2006, and ended on October 27, 2006, with the 83-win underdog Cardinals upsetting the heavily favored Tigers in five games in the 2006 World Series. Photo: Jleybov (CC BY-SA 2.5).

item.title: 2005: Eldred Announces Retirement as a Player
item.description: Eldred announced his retirement as a player on October 27, 2005. Photo: Keith Allison from Hanover, MD, USA (CC BY-SA 2.0).

item.title: 2004: Red Sox Sweep Cardinals, Win First World Series Since 1918
item.description: The Boston Red Sox complete a four-game sweep of the St. Louis Cardinals to win the World Series for the first time since 1918. Photo: Schmiddy at en.wikipedia (CC BY-SA 3.0).

item.title: 2002: Angels Win First World Series, Beat Giants 4-1 in Game 7
item.description: The Anaheim Angels win their first World Series as they defeat the San Francisco Giants 4–1 in Game Seven. Pitcher John Lackey (with relief help from Brendan Donnelly, Francisco Rodríguez, and Troy Percival) becomes the first rookie to win a 7th game of a World Series since 1909.

item.title: 2001: World Series Begins After September 11 Postponements
item.description: After MLB games were postponed as a result of the September 11 attacks, the World Series began on October 27, 2001, which was, at the time, the latest-ever start date for a World Series.

item.title: 1999: Yankees Beat Braves 4-1, Win Record 25th World Series
item.description: The New York Yankees defeat the Atlanta Braves, 4–1, to win their 25th World Series. Roger Clemens gets the win, hurling 4-hit ball before leaving the game in the 8th inning. Mariano Rivera gets the save, his second of the Series. Jim Leyritz hits a solo home run in the 8th inning to finish the NY scoring. Rivera wins the Series MVP award. Photo: User:Galaksiafervojo Muboshgu (CC BY-SA 3.0).

item.title: 1994: Jeff Bagwell Unanimously Wins NL MVP, First Astros Winner
item.description: Jeff Bagwell of the Houston Astros unanimously wins the National League MVP Award after getting all 28 first-place votes, becoming only the fourth unanimous MVP winner in NL history, and the first Astros player to win the award in franchise history. Photo: Mojo (CC BY 2.0).

item.title: 1992: Expansion Rockies Hire Don Baylor as First Manager
item.description: The expansion Colorado Rockies hire Don Baylor as the team's first manager. Photo: J. Elden Bailey on Flickr (original) CFIF (crop) (CC BY 2.0).

item.title: 1991: Twins Beat Braves 1-0 in 10 Innings, Win World Series
item.description: The Minnesota Twins become the 1991 World Series champions with a 1–0 victory behind Jack Morris' masterful 10-inning shutout. Gene Larkin's single off Atlanta Braves reliever Alejandro Peña scores Dan Gladden with the game's only run. The game is the first Game Seven to go into extra innings since the 1924 World Series between the Washington Senators and New York Giants. Photo: Arturo Pardavila III from Hoboken, NJ, USA (CC BY-SA 2.0).

item.title: 1989: Candlestick Park Hosts Game 3 After Ten-Day Quake Delay
item.description: After a ten-day postponement and a team of 17 engineers certifies its structural integrity, Candlestick Park finally hosts Game 3 of the World Series. A crowd of 62,038 honors those who died in the quake with a moment of silence and salutes first responders who saved lives throughout the region. Photo: Gateman1997 (talk) (CC BY-SA 3.0).

item.title: 1987: Buck Rodgers Elected NL Manager of the Year, Expos Win 91
item.description: Buck Rodgers, who led the Montreal Expos to 91 victories in 1987, is elected National League Manager of the Year by the BBWAA, outpacing Roger Craig of the San Francisco Giants by 27 points. Two days from now, Sparky Anderson of the American League East champion Detroit Tigers will win his second Junior Circuit Manager of the Year nod in four seasons, edging Tom Trebelhorn of the Milwaukee Brewers and Tom Kelly of… Photo: Unknown author (Public domain).

item.title: 1986: Mets Defeat Red Sox in Seven Games in 1986 World Series
item.description: The playoffs began on October 7, 1986, and concluded on October 27, 1986, with the Mets defeating the Red Sox in seven games in the 1986 World Series.

item.title: 1980: Astros Fire GM Tal Smith, Al Rosen Named Replacement
item.description: Two weeks after his Houston Astros post the best season in their 19-year history, and two weeks before he'll be named The Sporting News Executive of the Year, general manager Tal Smith is unceremoniously fired by Astros' principal owner John J. McMullen. Smith's GM post is immediately filled by former New York Yankees club president Al Rosen. Photo: EricEnfermero (CC BY-SA 4.0).

item.title: 1978: Bamberger Named AL Manager of the Year After 93-Win Brewers
item.description: George Bamberger of the Milwaukee Brewers is named the United Press International American League Manager of the Year. He guided the Brewers to 93 triumphs and the Brewers' first winning season. Bamberger receives 20 first-place votes to nine for Bob Lemon of the New York Yankees. Photo: Unknown author (Public domain).

item.title: 1977: Griffith Rejects Mauch's Request to Resign, Joins Angels
item.description: Calvin Griffith, owner of the Minnesota Twins, rejects manager Gene Mauch's request to resign and take a job as manager with the California Angels. Griffith informs Mauch and Angels owner Gene Autry that Mauch, a Southern California resident, is under contract to the Twins for three more years. Dave Garcia remains at the Angels' helm going into 1978.

item.title: 1971: Harry Dalton Hired as Angels General Manager
item.description: Baltimore Orioles general manager Harry Dalton is hired to fill Walsh's old job as GM of the California Angels. In his six years as head of baseball operations, Dalton's Orioles have won four American League pennants and two World Series titles. Executive vice president Frank Cashen assumes the Orioles' GM duties.

item.title: 1955: Clark Griffith, 85, Hall of Fame Pitcher and Manager
item.description: Clark Griffith, 85, Hall of Fame pitcher and manager, and principal owner of the Washington Senators since 1920; won 237 games in 20-year career in three major leagues between 1891 and 1914, with 20 or more victories in seven different campaigns; led National League in earned run average (1.88) in 1898, then was a key recruiter of NL players to upstart American League in 1901; managed Chicago White Stockings, New… Photo: National Photo Company Collection (Public domain).

item.title: 1950: Joe Gordon, 35, Released by Indians, Becomes Solons Player-Manager
item.description: Joe Gordon's 11-year big league playing career ends when he's released by the Cleveland Indians. The future Hall of Fame second baseman, 35, who won five World Series rings over that span, becomes the player-manager of the Sacramento Solons of the Pacific Coast League. Photo: Unknown (Public domain).

item.title: 1887: Brotherhood Players Refuse to Sign Contracts Until Salary Cap Deal
item.description: The Brotherhood of Professional Base-Ball Players agree to not sign contracts until an agreement has been reached with club owners regarding salary caps and the reserve rule.

item.title: 1877: Louisville Drops Four Players for Fixing Games, Forfeits Salaries
item.description: The Louisville Club formally drops Jim Devlin, George Hall, Al Nichols and Bill Craver for their involvement in the fixing of games. The players' remaining salaries are forfeited to the team. Devlin's testimony included statements that the team had paid umpire Dan Devinney (see August 6) extra to call games in Louisville's favor in roughly 20 games during the season. Photo: Scan by NYPL (Public domain).
